title: Diversity of Matter: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures (Basics)
topic: Exploring Diversity of Matter by its Chemical Composition
subject: Science

questions.question: Which statement best describes an element?
options: A substance made of two or more different types of atoms chemically combined
A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two or more substances not chemically combined
A substance that can be separated by physical means
questions.explanation: An element is a pure substance made of only one type of atom. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a compound?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
A substance made of two or more substances not chemically combined
A substance that displays properties of its constituents
questions.explanation: A compound consists of two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio. It has properties different from its constituent elements.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a mixture?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined
A substance made of two or more substances not chemically combined
A substance that cannot be separated by physical means
questions.explanation: A mixture contains two or more substances (elements or compounds) that are not chemically combined. They retain their individual properties.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an element?
questions.explanation: Iron is an element made of only iron atoms. Water and salt are compounds. Air is a mixture.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a compound?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a compound made of carbon and oxygen atoms chemically combined. Oxygen and gold are elements. Sea water is a mixture.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases like nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide. Copper is an element. Sugar and magnesium oxide are compounds.

questions.question: Which property is typical of most metals?
questions.explanation: Most metals are good conductors of electricity and heat. They are usually shiny and malleable, not brittle.

questions.question: Which property is typical of most non-metals?
questions.explanation: Most non-metals are poor conductors of electricity and heat. They are usually dull and brittle when solid.

questions.question: Where are metals mostly found in the Periodic Table?
options: On the left side and centre
questions.explanation: Metals are mostly located on the left side and centre of the Periodic Table. Non-metals are mostly on the right side.

questions.question: Can an element be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means?
questions.explanation: Elements are the simplest substances. They cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

questions.question: Do compounds have the same properties as the elements they are made from?
options: Only if the compound is a gas
questions.explanation: Compounds have completely different properties from their constituent elements. For example, sodium (metal) and chlorine (gas) form salt (edible solid).

questions.question: Do mixtures display the properties of their constituents?
options: Yes, they retain the properties of their constituents
No, they have completely new properties
Only the solid constituents retain properties
Only the liquid constituents retain properties
questions.explanation: Mixtures display the properties of their individual constituents because they are not chemically combined.

questions.question: Which of the following is a metal?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal. Sulfur, carbon, and oxygen are non-metals.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a non-metal. Iron, aluminium, and zinc are metals.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Carbon?
questions.explanation: The chemical symbol for Carbon is C. Ca is Calcium, Co is Cobalt, Cr is Chromium.

questions.question: In a compound, are the elements combined in a fixed ratio?
questions.explanation: Elements in a compound are always combined in a fixed ratio by mass. Mixtures have variable ratios.

questions.question: In a mixture, are the components combined in a fixed ratio?
questions.explanation: The components of a mixture can be mixed in any ratio. There is no fixed ratio.

questions.question: Is energy change usually involved when a compound is formed?
options: Yes, heat or light is often released or absorbed
Only if the compound is coloured
Only if the compound is a gas
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions to form compounds usually involve energy changes (heat, light, etc.). Mixing to form a mixture usually does not.

questions.question: Is oxygen gas (O2) an element or a compound?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is an element because it contains only one type of atom (oxygen), even though they are paired in molecules.

questions.question: Is salt water an element, compound or mixture?
questions.explanation: Salt water is a mixture of salt (compound) and water (compound). They are not chemically combined and can be separated.
